title: who manages nobody: four ways to ask, one of them wrong

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) AS manage_nobody
FROM employees AS e
WHERE e.id NOT IN (SELECT manager_id FROM employees)
steps.note: NOT IN: the CEO's NULL manager_id is in the list, so every id gets unknown. 0 rows.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) AS manage_nobody
FROM employees AS e
WHERE e.id NOT IN (SELECT manager_id FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL)
steps.note: NOT IN, with the NULLs filtered out of the subquery: the list has only real ids now. 200.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) AS manage_nobody
FROM employees AS e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees AS r WHERE r.manager_id = e.id)
steps.note: NOT EXISTS: is there an employee whose manager_id = e.id? the CEO's NULL just never matches. 200.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) AS manage_nobody
FROM employees AS e
LEFT JOIN employees AS r ON r.manager_id = e.id
WHERE r.id IS NULL
steps.note: LEFT JOIN, keep the padded rows: employees nobody reports to. 200.
